title: – VIP – Spying
audioPath: materials/Speak.Fluent.English china232/02Fluent VIP Pod/208 – VIP – Spying.mp3

dialog.speaker: A
dialog.text: Are you ok with the US government collecting all communications data like emails, phone call records, and things like Facebook messages?

dialog.speaker: B
dialog.text: No. I know they do it in the name of "National security" but they've gone way overboard. Who wants the government snooping around in your private emails and listening in on your phone calls? They have other ways to catch terrorists.

dialog.speaker: A
dialog.text: I think they can't listen in on the calls and only have access to theduration of the call. They can't check emails legally either without awarrant.

dialog.speaker: B
dialog.text: Ya, but who trusts them to abide by the law 100% of the time? I don't. We've seen this so many times. I think it's just a matter of time before the government starts to abuse it's power. They are doing everything behind closed doors and there is no transparency at all.

vocabulary.definition: If you do something "in the name of" something else, it means that you did it "because" of that. "Because" of course is used much more commonly, but "in the name of" still has a similar feel to it. Examples will give you an idea of when it's used. 2. She quit her job and moved to his country in the name of love.
This is a term that is used to describe things like the "military", the "FBI" and other government institutions that are supposed to help keep a country safe from terrorism or foreign invasion.

If you are "snooping around" it means you are "spying" on someone else's private stuff. If you are checking someone else's email, reading their diary, or looking around their bedroom for what they are hiding in there, you are "snooping around".

vocabulary.term: Stop snooping around my room. I need my privacy.

vocabulary.definition: This is kind of a "fancy" word for "how long or much time something takes". It says on the ticket that the duration of the flight is one hour.

Police who want to legally search someone's house need a "search warrent". A "warrent" is basically some type of special legal document from the government that allows people to do something they otherwise woudn't be able to do.
If you "abide by the law" it means that you follow and obey the law. You don't break the law and you don't do other illegal stuff.
If you do something "behind closed doors" it means that you do it in private and other people don't know what you are doing. It's private and secret.

"Transparency" means "see through". If you are talking about whether the government or a company is "transparent" or not, you are asking whether or not they share a lot of information or they keep most of it a secret. Anyone who keeps this information a secret is "not" being "transparent".
